clue.text: Boris yet to exercise temperance

indicators.note: to exercise something is to put it through its paces, working these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Boris has yet to take up moderation in drink, a jibe at a famously unrestrained politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance and sobriety are synonyms for restraint, especially in drinking alcohol.

clue.text: Suspect humming head off

indicators.note: with its head off, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: humming is British slang for smelling bad, as is niffy (from niff, a stink)

explanation.surface: A suspicious smell comes off someone's head, or a suspect is heading off.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain something 'humming' or 'niffy' smells unpleasant; chopping the N from NIFFY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something dubious or questionable is called suspect, the adjective sense of the slang word.

clue.text: Tearaway ultimately at fault

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: a fault is an error or mistake

explanation.surface: A reckless youngster is, in the end, the one to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is an unruly child, the sort informally called a little terror.

clue.text: Mischief and deadpan gags having malign influence

indicators.note: to gag is to stuff something into a mouth, so one word is packed inside another

parts.note: deadpan humour is dry
something with a malign influence is evil

explanation.surface: Pranks and straight-faced jokes are said to have a corrupting effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gags' reads as a noun, jokes, in the surface, but works as a verb: to gag is to stop up a mouth, so one word holds the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilry is wild, reckless mischief, behaviour worthy of an imp.

clue.text: Identical small females throwing tantrum

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: a tantrum throws everything into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Identical little girls are having a simultaneous meltdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing tantrum' is the anagram signal on the word females alone; the S for small stands outside it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfsame is an emphatic way of saying the very same, exactly alike.

clue.text: Cult's on-air broadcast not heard by us

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A cult's radio transmission goes unheard by the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters the letters of CULTSONAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound above the range of human hearing is described as beyond our ears, a high-frequency pitch.

clue.text: Serbia sedulously protecting partisan

indicators.note: the outer words protect the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: A Balkan country diligently shields a guerrilla fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partisan' looks like a noun for a resistance fighter, fitting Serbia, but here it is the adjective meaning one-sided.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan view is prejudiced, favouring one side rather than being neutral.

clue.text: Tory Right blocking liberal colleague

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: one piece blocks the other by standing in the middle of it

parts.note: liberal in the sense of unrestricted means free

explanation.surface: A right-wing Conservative obstructs a political opponent from the Liberal party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory' and 'liberal' suggest party politics; liberal here is just free.
explanation.definitionFit: A confrere is a fellow member of a profession, a peer or associate.

clue.text: He'd call regularly, bearing cake

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: a person's bearing is their air or manner

explanation.surface: Someone says he would visit often, bringing a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of HEDCALL, giving ECL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream, a small iced cake.

clue.text: Cases of Gewürztraminer, exceptionally pale

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so the outer letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Crates of a white wine are unusually light in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of Gewürztraminer give GR and of exceptionally give EY.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes something wan or colourless, like a pallid complexion.

clue.text: Destroying terrains of Amazonia, for example

indicators.note: destroying wrecks the order of these letters, which are rebuilt differently

explanation.surface: A lament for the land of the Amazon basin being wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroying' rearranges TERRAINSOF.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon basin is the world's largest tropical jungle, the prime example of this habitat.

clue.text: Soppy female and sheepish male

parts.note: soppy and wet both mean feeble or sentimental
HER is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A sentimental woman and a timid man make an odd couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheepish' seems to mean embarrassed but literally means of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A wether is a castrated ram, so literally a male of the flock.

clue.text: Attila upset retired nut gatherer

parts.note: Attila was the leader of the Huns, so he was the chief Hun

indicators.note: upset turns the word upside down, which in a down clue means reading it backwards

explanation.surface: The ruthless warlord overturns a squirrel that has given up foraging.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: nut is slang for the head, so one who collects heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A headhunter literally collects skulls of enemies; nut is slang for a person's cranium.

clue.text: Possibly lacking exercise, topless physique is classically epic

indicators.note: lacking means the following item is missing from the word

parts.note: possibly means perhaps
PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a physique is a body

explanation.surface: A flabby, bare-chested figure is described in grand heroic terms.
explanation.walkthrough: PERHAPS without PE gives RHAPS; BODY without its top letter gives ODY.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a rhapsody was an epic poem, or a section of one, recited in a single sitting.

clue.text: Generators died, rotating such a lot

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

indicators.note: rotating turns the words round so they read backwards

parts.note: such a lot means so many

explanation.surface: Power generators failed after spinning so much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotating' turns SO MANY into YNAMOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamos are machines converting mechanical energy into electrical current.

clue.text: Where wise creatures gather, spreading wise lore

indicators.note: spreading scatters these letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A place where the wise meet to share their learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges WISELORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are proverbially wise birds, and their roosts or haunts are where they congregate.

clue.text: Fixer full of limitless gas and wind

indicators.note: full of means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a fixer is a repairer, a mender

indicators.note: without limits, the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A repairman bloated with wind and gas, a comic image of indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' and 'wind' point to flatulence; wind here is the verb, as a river winds.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to twist and turn along a course, as a meandering river does.

clue.text: Settler perhaps restraining road rage

indicators.note: restraining means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: EG, for example, signals something offered as a possibility
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords
to rant is to rage loudly

explanation.surface: A colonist, perhaps, holding back fury at other drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler perhaps' looks like the definition, but 'perhaps' gives EG. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant leaves home to live in another country, becoming a colonist there.

clue.text: Tree, which reportedly gave girl optimism at last

indicators.note: reportedly signals a spoken version of the word, a homophone

parts.note: the word which is said aloud, sounding the same as the tree name's first part

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A tree, apparently, gave a girl hope in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The wych elm is a broad-leaved European species of elm.

clue.text: Allowed astronomer to leave Earth, with fatal consequences

parts.note: allowed means let

indicators.note: to leave means a letter departs from the word

parts.note: Edmond Halley was the astronomer after whom the comet is named

explanation.surface: An astronomer is permitted to leave the planet, and it ends in death.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethally means in a deadly manner, causing death.

clue.text: One turned up clutching £25 for Tom Jones?

indicators.note: clutching means holding the next piece inside
turned up in a down clue reverses the word, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: one, the impersonal pronoun, can stand for the speaker, me
pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: Someone appears gripping twenty-five pounds for the Welsh singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Jones seems to be the singer, but it is Fielding's novel, named after its hero; the question mark marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Jones is a title-giving character, a person whose name is given to a book or thing.

clue.text: Slick lie yielding students a sneaky day off

indicators.note: yielding means giving up, so these letters are removed

parts.note: L, for learner, stands for a student; two students give two

explanation.surface: A smooth fib lets students skip a day of school.
explanation.walkthrough: Both L's are removed from SLICKLIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickie is British slang for a day off work falsely claimed as sick leave.

clue.text: Group of musicians adjust private parts

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, letting another piece in

parts.note: to adjust a clock is to set it
PTE is the abbreviation for private, the army rank

explanation.surface: An instruction to rearrange one's intimate anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private parts' reads as a euphemism; private is a soldier and parts a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is an ensemble of seven performers.

clue.text: Local store fleeced a policeman, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: fleeced means shorn, followed by a as written
a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood shop has ripped off a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of SHORN A COP gives CORNA SHOP, said like the answer in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A local can mean a nearby small shop selling everyday groceries, often on a street junction.

clue.text: Run into revolting boozer and belch

indicators.note: into means placing one piece inside another
revolting turns the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a disgusting bar and lets out a burp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgusting but signals turning over.
explanation.definitionFit: A belch is an audible release of gas from the stomach through the mouth.

clue.text: Brahms and Liszt refusing to defect

indicators.note: refusing means turning away the following word, so it is removed

parts.note: Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk, as is blotto

explanation.surface: Two composers decline to change sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defect' looks like a verb about switching allegiance but is the noun, a flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot is a stain or blemish, a flaw on a reputation or page.

clue.text: Thinner axes bend, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word as spoken, a homophone

parts.note: the axes of a graph are X and Y, and to bend is to lean

explanation.surface: A slimmer person reports that hatchets are bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thinner' wants to be a comparative adjective; it is a paint solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylene is a hydrocarbon solvent used to dilute paints and varnishes.

clue.text: Idle criminal has siestas

indicators.note: something criminal is bent, so these letters are twisted

parts.note: to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: A lazy crook takes afternoon naps.
explanation.definitionFit: Siestas are short afternoon rests, naps taken during the day.
